# Overview

This workflow redesigns the Post-Breeding analysis so that the variables
that **define** the foraging strategies are kept separate from the
variables used to **test** and **characterise** them. (Robustness of the
number of dimensions and clusters is in
`NESE_HCPC_PostBreeding_Robustness.Rmd`.)

| Step | What | Role |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 2 | MFA (space + diving blocks, equal weight) + HCPC | defines strategies |
| 3 | Gaussian mixture on the MFA space | membership probabilities |
| 4 | Isotopes, mass gain, trip duration, morphology, year | **independent** validation |
| 5 | Repeat seals (PB–PB, PB→PM) | individual consistency |
| 6.1 | Isotopic niche (nicheROVER, SEA) | **independent** niche comparison |
| 6.2 | Spatial niche (utilisation distributions) | descriptive |
| 6.3 | Diving niche | descriptive |
| 6.4 | Null model for niche overlap | quantifies circularity |

Stable isotopes, mass gain and trip duration are **not** used to build
the clusters, so differences in them are genuine tests. Spatial and
diving niches are partly determined by the clustering itself and are
reported as descriptions, with a null model (6.4) showing how much
overlap would be expected from clustering alone.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(FactoMineR)
library(cluster)     # clusGap, silhouette
library(mclust)      # Mclust, adjustedRandIndex
library(nicheROVER)
library(sf)
# MASS is used with MASS:: to avoid masking dplyr::select
```

## Settings

```{r settings}
SEED         <- 20261102
K            <- 3        # number of strategies (see robustness Rmd)
N_DIM        <- 4        # MFA dimensions used for clustering (parallel analysis / broken stick)
N_BOOT       <- 500      # bootstrap replicates for cluster stability
N_PERM       <- 4999     # permutations for Freedman-Lane tests
N_POST       <- 1e4      # nicheROVER posterior draws
N_SIM        <- 200      # simulations for the overlap null model
UNCERTAIN_Z  <- 0.80     # seals with max membership probability below this are "uncertain"

# Equivalence margins (permil) for "the two offshore strategies feed at the same
# isotopic position". These are a biological judgement: justify them in the
# paper (e.g. inter-annual baseline variability, or a fraction of a 3-3.5 permil
# trophic step for d15N).
EQUIV <- c(d13C = 0.3, d15N = 0.5)

# Spatial utilisation distributions
LAEA             <- "+proj=laea +lat_0=45 +lon_0=-140 +units=km +datum=WGS84"
COLONY_LONLAT    <- c(-122.33, 37.11)   # Año Nuevo
COLONY_BUFFER_KM <- 100                 # drop locations near the colony (as in track2KBA tripSplit)
KERNEL_SD_KM     <- 50                  # kernel standard deviation (common to all seals)
KERNEL_SD_SENS   <- c(25, 50, 100)      # bandwidth sensitivity
CELL_KM          <- 25

OUT <- "../results/strategies_validation"
FIG <- "../figures/strategies_validation"
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(FIG, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(SEED)
```

## Data checks

```{r checks}
# Mesoecoregion proportions are compositional (sum to 1): one is redundant.
summary(rowSums(dat[grep("MesoEco", SPACE, value = TRUE)]))
# Dive-type percentages do NOT always sum to ~100: check the definition
# (unclassified dives?) before interpreting them.
summary(rowSums(dat[c("Pct_TransitDives", "Pct_ForagingDives",
                      "Pct_DriftDives", "Pct_BenthicDives")]))
# Highly redundant pairs (|Spearman rho| > 0.85)
rho <- cor(dat[BEHAV], method = "spearman"); rho[upper.tri(rho, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
as.data.frame(as.table(rho)) %>% filter(abs(Freq) > 0.85) %>% arrange(desc(abs(Freq)))
# Mass gain rate is correlated with trip duration: duration is a covariate below
cor.test(dat$MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker, dat$TripDuration_days, method = "spearman")
```

## Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# MFA on the behavioural blocks; isotopes optionally as a supplementary group
mfa_fit <- function(d, ncp = N_DIM, sup_iso = TRUE, ind.sup = NULL) {
  base <- d[, c(SPACE, DIVE, if (sup_iso) ISO)]
  rownames(base) <- NULL
  MFA(base,
      group = c(length(SPACE), length(DIVE), if (sup_iso) length(ISO)),
      type = rep("s", 2 + sup_iso),
      name.group = c("Space", "Diving", if (sup_iso) "Isotopes"),
      num.group.sup = if (sup_iso) 3 else NULL,
      ind.sup = ind.sup, ncp = ncp, graph = FALSE)
}
mfa_coords <- function(d, ncp = N_DIM) mfa_fit(d, ncp, sup_iso = FALSE)$ind$coord[, 1:ncp, drop = FALSE]

# Ward + k-means consolidation (= FactoMineR::HCPC), fast enough for loops
hcpc_lite <- function(S, k) {
  cl  <- cutree(hclust(dist(S), method = "ward.D2"), k)
  cen <- apply(S, 2, function(x) tapply(x, cl, mean))
  kmeans(S, centers = cen, iter.max = 100)$cluster
}
# HCPC automatic rule: minimise W(k)/W(k-1)
hcpc_ratio <- function(S, kmin = 2, kmax = 8) {
  h <- hclust(dist(S), method = "ward.D2")
  g <- sort(h$height^2 / (2 * nrow(S)), decreasing = TRUE)
  W <- sapply(1:(kmax + 1), function(k) sum(g[k:length(g)]))
  setNames(W[kmin:kmax] / W[(kmin - 1):(kmax - 1)], kmin:kmax)
}

# Relabel a partition so its labels match a reference partition as closely as possible
perms <- function(v) if (length(v) <= 1) list(v) else
  do.call(c, lapply(seq_along(v), function(i) lapply(perms(v[-i]), function(p) c(v[i], p))))
align_map <- function(new, ref) {        # returns map: map[new_label] = ref_label
  k <- max(new, ref)
  tab <- table(factor(new, 1:k), factor(ref, 1:k))
  P <- perms(1:k)
  P[[which.max(sapply(P, function(p) sum(tab[cbind(1:k, p)])))]]
}

# Freedman-Lane permutation F test for `term`, adjusting for `covars`
fl_test <- function(d, response, term = "strategy", covars = character(0), B = N_PERM) {
  v  <- c(response, term, covars)
  d  <- d[complete.cases(d[v]), v, drop = FALSE]
  X0 <- model.matrix(reformulate(if (length(covars)) covars else "1"), d)
  X1 <- model.matrix(reformulate(c(covars, term)), d)
  y  <- d[[response]]
  Fstat <- function(y) {
    m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); m1 <- lm.fit(X1, y)
    r0 <- sum(m0$residuals^2); r1 <- sum(m1$residuals^2)
    ((r0 - r1) / (m1$rank - m0$rank)) / (r1 / (nrow(X1) - m1$rank))
  }
  F_obs <- Fstat(y)
  m0  <- lm.fit(X0, y); fit0 <- y - m0$residuals
  F_p <- replicate(B, Fstat(fit0 + sample(m0$residuals)))
  data.frame(response = response,
             covariates = if (length(covars)) paste(covars, collapse = " + ") else "none",
             n = nrow(d), F = F_obs, p_perm = (1 + sum(F_p >= F_obs)) / (B + 1))
}

# All pairwise contrasts between levels of `term` from an lm, with CIs
pair_contrasts <- function(fit, term = "strategy", level = 0.95) {
  b <- coef(fit); V <- vcov(fit)
  lev <- levels(model.frame(fit)[[term]]); cn <- paste0(term, lev)
  tq <- qt(1 - (1 - level) / 2, fit$df.residual)
  do.call(rbind, combn(seq_along(lev), 2, simplify = FALSE, FUN = function(ij) {
    L <- setNames(numeric(length(b)), names(b))
    if (cn[ij[2]] %in% names(b)) L[cn[ij[2]]] <- 1
    if (cn[ij[1]] %in% names(b)) L[cn[ij[1]]] <- L[cn[ij[1]]] - 1
    est <- sum(L * b); se <- sqrt(drop(t(L) %*% V %*% L))
    data.frame(contrast = paste(lev[ij[2]], "-", lev[ij[1]]),
               estimate = est, lwr = est - tq * se, upr = est + tq * se)
  }))
}

# Plug-in Monte Carlo overlap: P(draw from niche i falls in alpha-region of niche j)
plugin_overlap <- function(S, cl, alpha = 0.95, N = 5000) {
  S <- as.matrix(S); cl <- as.character(cl); g <- sort(unique(cl)); q <- qchisq(alpha, ncol(S))
  par <- lapply(g, function(k) list(mu = colMeans(S[cl == k, , drop = FALSE]),
                                    Sig = cov(S[cl == k, , drop = FALSE])))
  O <- matrix(NA, length(g), length(g), dimnames = list(g, g))
  for (i in seq_along(g)) {
    Y <- MASS::mvrnorm(N, par[[i]]$mu, par[[i]]$Sig)
    for (j in seq_along(g)) O[i, j] <- mean(mahalanobis(Y, par[[j]]$mu, par[[j]]$Sig) <= q)
  }
  O
}
offdiag_mean <- function(O) mean(O[row(O) != col(O)])
```

# Defining the strategies: MFA on space + diving

Multiple Factor Analysis weights each block by the inverse of its first
eigenvalue, so the spatial (8 variables) and diving (11 variables)
blocks contribute equally, however many variables were measured in each.
Isotopes are projected as a **supplementary** group: they are shown on
the factor map but do not influence the solution.

```{r mfa}
res.mfa <- mfa_fit(dat, ncp = N_DIM)
round(head(res.mfa$eig, 8), 3)
res.mfa$group$RV          # similarity between blocks (incl. supplementary isotopes)
round(res.mfa$group$contrib, 1)
round(res.mfa$quanti.var.sup$cor, 2)   # isotopes vs MFA dimensions
S <- res.mfa$ind$coord[, 1:N_DIM]
```

## Number of clusters on the MFA space

```{r k-check}
round(hcpc_ratio(S), 3)        # HCPC rule (minimum = suggested k)
gs <- clusGap(S, FUNcluster = function(x, k) list(cluster = hcpc_lite(x, k)),
              K.max = 8, B = 200, spaceH0 = "scaledPCA", verbose = FALSE)
cat("Gap statistic (Tibshirani 1-SE) k =",
    maxSE(gs$Tab[, "gap"], gs$Tab[, "SE.sim"], method = "Tibs2001SEmax"), "\n")
sapply(2:6, function(k) c(k = k, min_size = min(table(hcpc_lite(S, k))),
                          silhouette = round(mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(S, k), dist(S))[, 3]), 3)))
```

## HCPC and comparison with the original PCA solution

```{r hcpc}
res.hcpc <- HCPC(res.mfa, nb.clust = K, consol = TRUE, graph = FALSE)
cl_raw <- as.integer(res.hcpc$data.clust$clust)

# Label strategies to match the original cluster numbers where possible
map <- if (all(!is.na(dat$orig_cluster))) align_map(cl_raw, dat$orig_cluster) else 1:K
dat$strategy <- factor(paste0("C", map[cl_raw]), levels = paste0("C", 1:K))
table(dat$strategy)
cat("ARI with original PCA-HCPC clusters:",
    round(adjustedRandIndex(dat$strategy, dat$orig_cluster), 3), "\n")

# Which strategy is coastal? (highest California Current use)
COASTAL <- names(which.max(tapply(dat$MesoEcoProportionCAC, dat$strategy, mean)))
OFFSHORE <- setdiff(levels(dat$strategy), COASTAL)
dat %>% group_by(strategy) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(grep("MesoEco", SPACE, value = TRUE), ~ round(mean(.x), 2)))
```

## Cluster stability (whole-pipeline bootstrap)

Each replicate resamples seals and re-runs MFA + clustering. Mean
Jaccard \> 0.75 = stable, \> 0.85 = highly stable, \< 0.5 = dissolved
(Hennig 2007).

```{r jaccard}
ref <- as.integer(dat$strategy)
J <- matrix(NA, N_BOOT, K)
for (b in 1:N_BOOT) {
  ix <- unique(sample(n, replace = TRUE))
  cb <- hcpc_lite(mfa_coords(dat[ix, ]), K)
  for (c in 1:K) {
    A <- ix[ref[ix] == c]
    if (length(A)) J[b, c] <- max(sapply(unique(cb), function(j) {
      Bj <- ix[cb == j]; length(intersect(A, Bj)) / length(union(A, Bj)) }))
  }
}
jac <- data.frame(strategy = levels(dat$strategy), n = as.vector(table(dat$strategy)),
                  jaccard_mean = colMeans(J, na.rm = TRUE),
                  P_dissolved = colMeans(J < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE))
jac
write.csv(jac, file.path(OUT, "jaccard_MFA.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Membership probabilities (Gaussian mixture)

Hard clusters hide how confidently each seal is assigned. A Gaussian
mixture fitted to the same MFA space gives each seal a probability of
belonging to each strategy. BIC over G = 1–6 is shown for information;
the K-component model is used for membership.

```{r mclust}
summary(mclustBIC(S, G = 1:6))
mc <- Mclust(S, G = K)
cat("Covariance model:", mc$modelName, "\n")
mmap <- align_map(mc$classification, as.integer(dat$strategy))
z <- matrix(NA, n, K, dimnames = list(dat$TOPPID, levels(dat$strategy)))
z[, mmap] <- mc$z
dat$p_member <- z[cbind(1:n, as.integer(dat$strategy))]   # prob. of own (HCPC) strategy
dat$mc_strategy <- factor(levels(dat$strategy)[mmap[mc$classification]], levels(dat$strategy))
table(HCPC = dat$strategy, Mixture = dat$mc_strategy)
dat %>% group_by(strategy) %>%
  summarise(median_p = median(p_member), n_uncertain = sum(p_member < UNCERTAIN_Z))
dat %>% filter(p_member < UNCERTAIN_Z) %>%
  dplyr::select(TOPPID, ProcedureYear, strategy, mc_strategy, p_member)
write.csv(data.frame(TOPPID = dat$TOPPID, strategy = dat$strategy, round(z, 3)),
          file.path(OUT, "membership_probabilities.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Independent validation

None of these variables were used to define the strategies. Tests are
Freedman–Lane permutation F tests (robust to non-normality and to the
small coastal group), with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across the
family. Year is a covariate for isotopes (baseline variation) and mass
gain; trip duration is a covariate for mass gain rate.

```{r validation}
val_specs <- list(
  list("d13C", character(0)), list("d13C", "ProcedureYear"),
  list("d15N", character(0)), list("d15N", "ProcedureYear"),
  list("MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker", character(0)),
  list("MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker", "TripDuration_days"),
  list("MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker", c("TripDuration_days", "ProcedureYear")),
  list("TripDuration_days", character(0)),
  list("AgeDeploy", character(0)),
  list("StandardLength_cm", character(0)),
  list("Mass_Procedure_kg", character(0)))

run_validation <- function(d) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  out <- do.call(rbind, lapply(val_specs, function(s) fl_test(d, s[[1]], covars = s[[2]])))
  out$p_BH <- p.adjust(out$p_perm, "BH")
  out
}
val <- run_validation(dat)
val %>% mutate(across(c(F, p_perm, p_BH), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
write.csv(val, file.path(OUT, "validation_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

dat %>% group_by(strategy) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(c(d13C, d15N, MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker, TripDuration_days,
                              AgeDeploy, StandardLength_cm, Mass_Procedure_kg),
                            ~ round(median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 2)))
```

## Effect sizes

```{r contrasts}
fits <- list(
  d13C      = lm(d13C ~ strategy + ProcedureYear, dat),
  d15N      = lm(d15N ~ strategy + ProcedureYear, dat),
  mass_gain = lm(MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker ~ strategy + TripDuration_days + ProcedureYear, dat),
  duration  = lm(TripDuration_days ~ strategy, dat))
contr <- bind_rows(lapply(fits, pair_contrasts), .id = "response")
contr %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(contr, file.path(OUT, "validation_contrasts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Do the two offshore strategies share the same isotopic position? (equivalence)

Two one-sided tests (TOST): equivalence is supported if the 90 % CI of
the difference lies entirely within ±margin.

```{r equivalence}
tost <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  ci <- pair_contrasts(fits[[v]], level = 0.90)
  ci <- ci[ci$contrast == paste(OFFSHORE[2], "-", OFFSHORE[1]), ]
  data.frame(isotope = v, contrast = ci$contrast, estimate = ci$estimate,
             lwr90 = ci$lwr, upr90 = ci$upr, margin = EQUIV[[v]],
             equivalent = ci$lwr > -EQUIV[[v]] & ci$upr < EQUIV[[v]])
}))
tost %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## Sensitivity of the validation

```{r validation-sens}
# (a) One trip per seal (removes repeated individuals)
dat_one <- dat %>% arrange(ProcedureYear) %>% filter(is.na(MainID) | !duplicated(MainID))
val_one <- run_validation(dat_one)
# (b) Excluding seals with uncertain membership
val_cert <- run_validation(dat %>% filter(p_member >= UNCERTAIN_Z))
bind_rows(all = val, one_trip_per_seal = val_one, certain_only = val_cert, .id = "subset") %>%
  dplyr::select(subset, response, covariates, n, p_perm) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = subset, values_from = c(n, p_perm)) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("p_"), ~ signif(.x, 3)))

# (c) Mixed model with seal as random effect (optional)
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  m_mix <- lme4::lmer(MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker ~ strategy + TripDuration_days +
                        ProcedureYear + (1 | MainID), data = dat)
  print(summary(m_mix)$coefficients)
}
```

## Year

Three of the coastal seals are from 2014 (marine heatwave onset). Is
coastal foraging a strategy or a response to that year's conditions?

```{r year}
table(dat$strategy, dat$ProcedureYear)
fisher.test(table(dat$strategy, dat$ProcedureYear), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4)
fisher.test(table(coastal = dat$strategy == COASTAL, y2014 = dat$ProcedureYear == "2014"))
```

# Individual consistency

## Seals tracked on two Post-Breeding trips

```{r consistency-pb}
rep_pb <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(MainID)) %>% group_by(MainID) %>% filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(MainID, ProcedureYear) %>%
  dplyr::select(MainID, TOPPID, ProcedureYear, strategy, p_member)
rep_pb
n_same <- rep_pb %>% summarise(same = n_distinct(strategy) == 1) %>% pull(same) %>% sum()
n_rep  <- n_distinct(rep_pb$MainID)
# Null: shuffle strategy labels across all trips
null_same <- replicate(N_PERM, {
  s <- sample(dat$strategy); names(s) <- dat$TOPPID
  sum(tapply(s[rep_pb$TOPPID], rep_pb$MainID, function(x) n_distinct(x) == 1))
})
cat(n_same, "of", n_rep, "repeat seals kept their strategy; expected by chance",
    round(mean(null_same), 2), "; P =", round((1 + sum(null_same >= n_same)) / (N_PERM + 1), 4), "\n")
```

## Post-Breeding → Post-Molt (exploratory)

Post-Molt trips of the same seals are projected into the Post-Breeding
MFA space as supplementary individuals and assigned with the mixture
model. Post- Molt trips are longer and in a different season, so a
change of strategy is not necessarily inconsistency; treat as
exploratory.

```{r consistency-pm}
pm <- all_trips %>% filter(Trip == "PostMolt", !is.na(MainID), MainID %in% dat$MainID) %>%
  filter(complete.cases(across(all_of(BEHAV)))) %>% as.data.frame()
if (nrow(pm) > 0) {
  both <- rbind(dat[, c(SPACE, DIVE)], pm[, c(SPACE, DIVE)])
  res.sup <- mfa_fit(both, ncp = N_DIM, sup_iso = FALSE, ind.sup = (n + 1):(n + nrow(pm)))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(abs(unname(res.sup$ind$coord[, 1:N_DIM])), abs(unname(S)))))
  # MFA axes can flip sign between fits: align supplementary coordinates to S
  sgn <- sign(colSums(res.sup$ind$coord[, 1:N_DIM] * S))
  S_pm <- sweep(res.sup$ind.sup$coord[, 1:N_DIM, drop = FALSE], 2, sgn, "*")
  pr <- predict(mc, newdata = S_pm)
  pm$pred <- factor(levels(dat$strategy)[mmap[pr$classification]], levels(dat$strategy))
  pm$p_pred <- apply(pr$z, 1, max)
  pb_strat <- dat %>% arrange(ProcedureYear) %>% distinct(MainID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::select(MainID, PB_strategy = strategy)
  pm_cmp <- pm %>% dplyr::select(MainID, TOPPID, ProcedureYear, PM_assigned = pred, p_pred) %>%
    left_join(pb_strat, by = "MainID")
  print(pm_cmp)
  print(table(PB = pm_cmp$PB_strategy, PM = pm_cmp$PM_assigned))
}
```

# Niches by domain

## Isotopic niche (independent of the clustering)

nicheROVER with its default (non-informative) prior, in δ¹³C–δ¹⁵N space.
Bayesian standard ellipse area (SEA_B) is computed from the same
posterior (area of the 40 % ellipse, π√\|Σ\|), and SEAc
(small-sample-corrected) from the data, so SIBER/JAGS are not required.

```{r iso-niche}
set.seed(SEED)
iso.par <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy,
                  function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = N_POST, X = as.matrix(dat[ii, ISO])))

iso.size95 <- sapply(iso.par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = 0.95))
sea.b      <- sapply(iso.par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, function(Sg) pi * sqrt(det(Sg))))
sea.c      <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy, function(ii) {
  m <- length(ii); pi * sqrt(det(cov(dat[ii, ISO]))) * (m - 1) / (m - 2) })

iso_sizes <- data.frame(strategy = colnames(sea.b), n = as.vector(table(dat$strategy)),
  SEAc = as.vector(sea.c),
  SEAb_median = apply(sea.b, 2, median),
  SEAb_lwr = apply(sea.b, 2, quantile, 0.025), SEAb_upr = apply(sea.b, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  NR95_median = apply(iso.size95, 2, median))
iso_sizes %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
# Posterior probability that one strategy's SEA_B is larger than another's
outer(colnames(sea.b), colnames(sea.b),
      Vectorize(function(a, b) round(mean(sea.b[, a] > sea.b[, b]), 3))) %>%
  `dimnames<-`(list(colnames(sea.b), colnames(sea.b)))

set.seed(SEED)
iso.over <- overlap(iso.par, nreps = 1e4, nprob = 1e4, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))
iso.over.mean <- apply(iso.over, c(1:2, 4), mean) * 100
iso.over.ci   <- apply(iso.over * 100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
round(iso.over.mean[, , 1], 1)   # 95% niche region: P(row in column's niche), %
round(iso.over.ci[, , , 1], 1)
write.csv(iso_sizes, file.path(OUT, "isotopic_niche_size.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r iso-plots, fig.height = 6}
clrs <- c("#7570b3", "#1b9e77", "#d95f02")[1:K]
set.seed(SEED)
iso.par50 <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy,
                    function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = 50, X = as.matrix(dat[ii, ISO])))
iso.data  <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy, function(ii) as.matrix(dat[ii, ISO]))
niche.plot(niche.par = iso.par50, niche.data = iso.data, pfrac = 0.05,
           iso.names = expression(delta^{13}*C, delta^{15}*N), col = clrs)
overlap.plot(iso.over[, , , 1], col = clrs, mean.cred.col = "turquoise", equal.axis = TRUE,
             xlab = "Overlap probability (%) - 95% isotopic niche region")
```

**Caveats.** Isotope baselines vary among years; if the year effect in
Section 4 is large, repeat with year-centred isotopes (below),
remembering that centring also removes any real strategy difference
confounded with year (e.g. coastal seals in 2014). Also state which
tissue was sampled and the time window it integrates relative to the
tracked trip.

```{r iso-yearcentred}
iso_c <- dat %>% group_by(ProcedureYear) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ISO), ~ .x - mean(.x))) %>% ungroup() %>% as.data.frame()
set.seed(SEED)
iso.par.c <- tapply(seq_len(n), iso_c$strategy,
                    function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = N_POST, X = as.matrix(iso_c[ii, ISO])))
round(apply(overlap(iso.par.c, nreps = 5000, nprob = 5000, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99)),
            c(1:2, 4), mean)[, , 1] * 100, 1)
```

## Spatial niche (descriptive)

One kernel utilisation distribution (UD) per seal on a common equal-area
grid and a common bandwidth; the strategy UD is the mean of its seals'
UDs, so each seal has equal weight regardless of track length. Overlap
is measured with Bhattacharyya's affinity (BA; 0 = none, 1 = identical)
and UDOI on the 95 % isopleths (Fieberg & Kochanny 2005). Because
spatial variables helped define the strategies, low between-strategy
overlap is expected and is a description, not a test. The
individual-level BA (within vs between strategies) shows how tightly
seals within a strategy share space.

```{r tracks}
tracks <- read.csv("../data/NESETracks6h.csv") %>%
  filter(Season == "PB") %>%
  mutate(TOPPID = as.character(track_id),
         longitude = ifelse(longitude > 180, longitude - 360, longitude)) %>%
  inner_join(dat %>% dplyr::select(TOPPID, strategy), by = "TOPPID")

xy  <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_as_sf(tracks, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                                            crs = 4326), LAEA))
col <- st_coordinates(st_transform(st_sfc(st_point(COLONY_LONLAT), crs = 4326), LAEA))
tracks <- tracks %>% mutate(x = xy[, 1], y = xy[, 2],
                            d_col = sqrt((x - col[1])^2 + (y - col[2])^2)) %>%
  filter(d_col > COLONY_BUFFER_KM) %>%
  group_by(TOPPID) %>% filter(n() >= 10) %>% ungroup()
seals <- tracks %>% distinct(TOPPID, strategy)
cat(nrow(seals), "seals with tracks;", nrow(tracks), "at-sea locations\n")
table(seals$strategy)

pad  <- 3 * max(KERNEL_SD_SENS)
lims <- c(range(tracks$x) + c(-pad, pad), range(tracks$y) + c(-pad, pad))
nx <- ceiling(diff(lims[1:2]) / CELL_KM) + 1
ny <- ceiling(diff(lims[3:4]) / CELL_KM) + 1
grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(lims[1], lims[2], length.out = nx),
                    y = seq(lims[3], lims[4], length.out = ny))

# Individual UDs: one column per seal, cells as rows, each column sums to 1
# (MASS::kde2d uses a Gaussian kernel with sd = h/4)
ud_individual <- function(sd_km) {
  sapply(seals$TOPPID, function(id) {
    tr <- tracks[tracks$TOPPID == id, ]
    z  <- as.vector(MASS::kde2d(tr$x, tr$y, h = 4 * sd_km, n = c(nx, ny), lims = lims)$z)
    z / sum(z)
  })
}
in_isopleth <- function(p, level) {
  o <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE); keep <- logical(length(p))
  keep[o[cumsum(p[o]) <= level]] <- TRUE; keep
}
udoi <- function(p1, p2, level = 0.95) {
  a <- in_isopleth(p1, level) & in_isopleth(p2, level)
  sum(a) * sum(p1[a] * p2[a])
}
strategy_overlap <- function(P) {
  U <- sapply(levels(dat$strategy), function(s) rowMeans(P[, seals$strategy == s, drop = FALSE]))
  BA <- crossprod(sqrt(U))
  UO <- outer(colnames(U), colnames(U), Vectorize(function(a, b) udoi(U[, a], U[, b])))
  dimnames(UO) <- dimnames(BA)
  list(U = U, BA = BA, UDOI = UO)
}
```

```{r spatial-overlap}
P  <- ud_individual(KERNEL_SD_KM)
so <- strategy_overlap(P)
round(so$BA, 3)
round(so$UDOI, 3)

# Bandwidth sensitivity
sapply(KERNEL_SD_SENS, function(h) {
  o <- strategy_overlap(if (h == KERNEL_SD_KM) P else ud_individual(h))$BA
  o[upper.tri(o)]
}) %>% `colnames<-`(paste0("sd_", KERNEL_SD_SENS, "km")) %>%
  `rownames<-`(combn(levels(dat$strategy), 2, paste, collapse = "-")) %>% round(3)

# Individual-level overlap: within vs between strategies
BAi <- crossprod(sqrt(P))
pairs <- which(upper.tri(BAi), arr.ind = TRUE)
ind_ba <- data.frame(s1 = seals$strategy[pairs[, 1]], s2 = seals$strategy[pairs[, 2]],
                     BA = BAi[pairs]) %>%
  mutate(pair = ifelse(s1 == s2, paste(s1, "(within)"),
                       paste(pmin(as.character(s1), as.character(s2)),
                             pmax(as.character(s1), as.character(s2)), sep = "-")))
ind_ba %>% group_by(pair) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs = n(), median_BA = median(BA), q25 = quantile(BA, .25), q75 = quantile(BA, .75))
write.csv(round(so$BA, 4), file.path(OUT, "spatial_BA_strategies.csv"))
```

```{r spatial-map, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
iso_vol <- function(p) { o <- order(p, decreasing = TRUE); v <- numeric(length(p)); v[o] <- cumsum(p[o]); v }
map_df <- bind_rows(lapply(colnames(so$U), function(s)
  cbind(grid, strategy = s, vol = iso_vol(so$U[, s]))))
gmap <- ggplot(map_df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = vol, colour = strategy, linetype = after_stat(factor(level))),
               breaks = c(0.5, 0.95)) +
  geom_point(data = data.frame(x = col[1], y = col[2]), shape = 17, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(clrs, levels(dat$strategy))) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(1, 2), labels = c("50%", "95%"), name = "Isopleth") +
  coord_equal() + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Easting (km, LAEA)", y = "Northing (km, LAEA)",
       title = "Strategy utilisation distributions (equal weight per seal)")
gmap
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "strategy_UDs.pdf"), gmap, width = 7, height = 6)
```

## Diving niche (descriptive)

PCA of the diving variables alone; nicheROVER in the first two diving
PCs.

```{r dive-niche}
pca_dive <- prcomp(dat[DIVE], scale. = TRUE)
summary(pca_dive)$importance[, 1:4]
round(pca_dive$rotation[, 1:2], 2)
D2 <- pca_dive$x[, 1:2]
set.seed(SEED)
dive.par <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy, function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = N_POST, X = D2[ii, ]))
dive.size <- sapply(dive.par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = 0.95))
round(apply(dive.size, 2, quantile, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)), 2)
set.seed(SEED)
dive.over <- overlap(dive.par, nreps = 1e4, nprob = 1e4, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))
round(apply(dive.over, c(1:2, 4), mean)[, , 1] * 100, 1)
```

## How much overlap does clustering alone create? (null model)

Seals are simulated from a single multivariate normal with the observed
correlation among the 19 behavioural variables — no strategies — then
run through the same pipeline (MFA → K clusters). The overlap between
these artificial clusters is what would be found even if strategies did
not exist. Observed overlaps are computed with the same plug-in
estimator so they are directly comparable. The comparison is made for
(i) the MFA space — the kind of space the original nicheROVER analysis
used — and (ii) the diving-PC space. Isotopic niches need no null:
isotopes were not used for clustering.

```{r null-overlap}
R_behav <- cor(dat[BEHAV])
summ <- function(O, cl) {   # mean off-diagonal overlap and the two largest clusters' mutual overlap
  big <- names(sort(table(cl), decreasing = TRUE))[1:2]
  c(mean_offdiag = offdiag_mean(O), largest_pair = mean(c(O[big[1], big[2]], O[big[2], big[1]])))
}
set.seed(SEED)
null <- t(replicate(N_SIM, {
  Z <- as.data.frame(MASS::mvrnorm(n, rep(0, ncol(R_behav)), R_behav)); names(Z) <- BEHAV
  Sz <- mfa_coords(Z); cl <- hcpc_lite(Sz, K)
  if (min(table(cl)) < 4) return(rep(NA_real_, 4))
  Dz <- prcomp(Z[DIVE], scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1:2]
  c(summ(plugin_overlap(Sz, cl), cl), summ(plugin_overlap(Dz, cl), cl))
}))
colnames(null) <- c("MFA_mean", "MFA_pair", "Dive_mean", "Dive_pair")

set.seed(SEED)
obs <- c(summ(plugin_overlap(S, dat$strategy), dat$strategy),
         summ(plugin_overlap(D2, dat$strategy), dat$strategy))
names(obs) <- colnames(null)
null_tab <- data.frame(statistic = names(obs), observed = obs,
  null_median = apply(null, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  null_lwr = apply(null, 2, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
  null_upr = apply(null, 2, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
  P_null_le_obs = sapply(names(obs), function(s) mean(null[, s] <= obs[s], na.rm = TRUE)))
null_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(null_tab, file.path(OUT, "overlap_null_model.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Interpretation: if the observed overlap is far below the null range, the
strategies are more distinct than clustering alone would produce. The
*size* of the null overlap shows why overlap in the clustering space
cannot by itself be reported as evidence of niche partitioning.
